instructions: Fresh review of each primary candidate: read dialogue first, then exact cards. Assess all six unchanged criteria and all coach-2.0 gates with turn-specific evidence. For pairs, show whether the Stance changes HOW A pursues the Drive in one interaction. Do not invent missing backstory or assume prior approval. Use the alternate only to assess meaningful differentiation. Report actual reservations. No writer scores or improvement claims are supplied.
productionStandard:
PRODUCTION STANDARD coach-2.0. Historical coach-1.0 acceptance is not coach-2.0 acceptance. Read the dialogue first and record what the spoken words establish before interpreting the card. Exact cards are already in this invocation: label internal-dialogue-first, never blind or human review. Do not invent a charitable backstory; harmless unspecified names/history are not defects. Fill coach2 for ORIGINAL dialogue in writer output and CANDIDATE dialogue in reviewer output. Copy the supplied dialogue hash for the text being assessed. Give concise actual turn evidence, not generic claims.
G1: legible immediate situation, wants/stakes; separate stated, ordinary inferred, and missing essentials. Identify first material defect or explicitly none.
G2: coherent facts, ownership, timing, language, knowledge; recognizable misunderstanding/revelation is allowed, unstated intervening events are not.
G3: assess all A1-B2, B2-A3, A3-B4, B4-A5 links. Vocabulary repetition alone is insufficient. Purposeful avoidance must read as behavior.
G4: B is a plausible participant with an intelligible practical/emotional position, not a contrived punchline cue. B can help, concede or solve.
G5: exact card changes A's choices. For pairs Stance changes HOW A pursues Drive and B responds to the merged behavior; neither card may be decorative.
G6: ending develops the same behavior using B4. Investigate if A5 would work after unrelated B4; more obstacles are not required for heightening.
format: five spoken ABABA turns, existing word/schema limit, no narration/coaching/truncation.
Every mandatory gate and transition is PASS, FAIL or UNCLEAR with evidence; UNCLEAR cannot be accepted. All gates pass AND total >=85 AND fidelity/response >=4 AND others >=3; preserve the six weights 30/20/15/15/10/10. A 5 is not merely presence. Totals are derived in code. Retain good originals; no rewrite quota. Review both alternatives for different tactics, relationships or pressure. Scene outline identifies roles, task, A want, B want, stakes, exact-card tactic and B's contribution; it is private planning evidence, not a substitute for missing spoken facts. Humour must come from sincere priorities and responsive choices, not stock hierarchy or unrelated slogans. Record actual weaknesses and reservations. Writer corrections target only rejected/materially changed scenes; preserve all accepted records and prior original assessments exactly. No coach-1.0 failure or exhausted allowance is erased by this separately versioned cycle.

cards.title: Act Like You Belong
cards.instruction: You do not understand what is happening. Copy the confidence around you and never admit confusion.

cards.title: What Really Happened?
cards.instruction: Find the truth by comparing details, repeating questions, and testing which parts of the story remain consistent.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm holding up two fingers too. Two parcels missing, then. You said a bag, then a box. Which went first?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I meant two things I remember: handles and a lid. There was only one parcel.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Two identifying features, certainly. Were the handles attached to fabric or cardboard?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Cardboard. But the box was inside a cloth bag.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: One parcel, two layers. Tell me again: when did you last see the box and bag together?

beats.text: You've put four beside the café, so I put four beside the bus. Two stops at four; that can't be right. Which story goes on your lost-bag claim?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Four's the bus number. I went into the café while it waited.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Route four, certainly. You said the bag was on the seat. Which seat?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The café chair. I paid, then ran for the bus.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Start from paying again. Did you reach down for the bag before you ran?

cards.instruction: You do not understand what is happening. Copy the confidence around you and never admit confusion.

cards.title: Back My Version
cards.instruction: Recruit someone to remember, repeat, and defend one shared version of events when questions begin.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've put tape on the greenhouse door like yours. Safe to go in, then. We'll tell the committee we came in after the glass broke.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Tape means keep out. Your wheelbarrow broke it before either of us went in.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly, before we went in. We both arrived inside to clear up. That's what we'll say.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll say we cleared up. I won't hide your wheelbarrow.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Mention moving it out of the way after the clearing up. Let's both tell it in that order.

beats.text: I've put a spoon upside down beside yours. Judges' tasting done. Remember, we both made this jam from scratch.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Mine's upside down because it's dirty. The jam still has the supermarket label on the jar.

cards.title: Test the Story First
cards.instruction: Get someone else to repeat the explanation, ask the dangerous question, or test the risky step before you commit.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You've turned your page over, so I've turned my accounts over. Anonymous questions, good. Ask the chair whether a banking delay explains the missing raffle money before I sign.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm using the blank side for sums. I'm not defending your accounts again.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Room for calculations, yes. Just ask her whether a banking delay is plausible.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She'll ask whose money.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Say you're testing a hypothetical. If she wants a name, come back before giving mine.

cards.title: Credit for the Discovery
cards.instruction: Make someone acknowledge that you found the clue, saw through the deception, or designed the successful scheme.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've circled the receipt number like you. Proof I've solved the missing-money problem. Put my name beside that in the report.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The circle means check it. We still need to see whether that payment went through twice.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Naturally, checking my discovery. Compare the bank entries under that number.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: There are two. I'll list everyone who helped find the duplicate.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: List them. Put 'found the receipt' beside my name, so I don't disappear into 'helped'.

beats.text: I've drawn a cross on the wall like yours. Doorway found. On tomorrow's tour, tell them it was my diagram.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: My cross marks a live wire. Mum stripped the plaster and found the actual doorway two feet to the left.

beats.speaker: A

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll let you open the door for the visitors.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Introduce me first. Otherwise I'll just be the one holding it.

cards.title: Truth or Loyalty
cards.instruction: Make someone choose between protecting the relationship and answering a dangerous question honestly.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: My hand's out too. A brothers' promise. Will you tell Mum I broke her vase, or keep it between us?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I was asking for the broken handle. She's blaming the cleaner.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The handle, yes. Take it and clear the cleaner without naming me.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She asked me directly whether you did it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then take my hand before you answer. Are we keeping this between brothers?
